owners.title: feat: GitHub Enterprise source links for repository evidence
owners.head: b06593763f5c3a041c3dde0391e89594b40d4788
owners.scope:
## Problem and value

Closes #1034.

A repository-backed diagram on a GitHub Enterprise host (GHE.com or a
self-managed GHES) cannot publish source links today. Web links are only built
for github.com, gitee.com and gitlab.com, or for a self-managed GitLab host
declared with `provider: "gitlab"` (#662). For any other host,
`provider: "github"` fails with `repository-evidence/provider-invalid`, so the
only way through is `link_mode: "local-only"`: verification still runs, but the
sources render as plain text instead of revision-pinned links.

GitHub Enterprise Server and GHE.com serve exactly the github.com URL layout
(`/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<rev>/<path>#L<a>-L<b>`, `/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<rev>`),
so no new link builder is needed — the declaration only has to be accepted, the
same way the accepted GitLab precedent accepts a declared self-managed host.

## What changed

- `archify/renderers/shared/repository-location.mjs`
  - `parseRepositoryRemote` now honours a `provider: "github"` hint on a host
    that is not github.com, mirroring the existing `provider: "gitlab"` hint.
    A public host still selects its provider automatically, and a declared
    provider that disagrees with a public host still fails
    `repository-evidence/provider-invalid`.
  - The returned location gained `publicHost` (whether the host is one of the
    known public forge hosts), so callers do not have to repeat the host table.
- `archify/renderers/shared/repository-evidence.mjs`
  - The evidence label keeps the host name for a declared GitHub Enterprise
    host (`ghe.example.com/Platform/evidence-repo`) instead of abbreviating to
    an owner/repository path that would read as a github.com repository. The
    label is rendered into every artifact, so github.com, gitee.com,
    gitlab.com, self-managed GitLab and `local-only` keep byte-identical
    labels.
  - The `provider-invalid` and `links-unsupported` diagnostics and their
    `supportedFixes` now name the GitHub Enterprise option, and state the two
    conditions that still reject such a host: a GitHub-family path is
    `owner/repository` on the standard HTTPS port (only GitLab names nested
    groups).
- `archify/references/authoring-contract.md` and
  `archify/references/repository-authoring.md` — the declaration, the
  `owner/repository` rule, the `#L<a>-L<b>` anchor and the `provider: "github"`
  entry in the local-only identity paragraph.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — an `### Added` entry under `## [Unreleased]`.
- `test/repository-evidence.test.mjs` — two new tests mirroring the
  self-managed GitLab tests: the accepted host (HTTPS, Git SSH, SSH URL and a
  case-variant path all match one repository, with the github.com link layout)
  and the guards that still apply (no declaration, a provider that disagrees
  with a public host, plain HTTP, a nested path, a non-standard port, and
  origins on another host or port). The existing github.com, gitee.com,
  gitlab.com and self-managed GitLab tests now pin the label bytes.
- `archify.zip` — rebuilt with the canonical Node 22 toolchain; two builds are
  byte-identical (sha256
  `76a6fe5048f8769a1fcae75826757c2fec8d8a1865908a6277eb2cad48001bb6`).

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-tests.mjs test/repository-evidence.test.mjs` — 34 pass,
  0 fail, 1 pre-existing platform skip.
- Red proof: with the provider hint reverted, exactly the two new tests fail
  (`repository-evidence/provider-invalid`); the 32 pre-existing tests still
  pass. Restored, the file is green again.
- `npm run test:generated` — all checks pass (viewer, brand marks, generated
  validators, release identity, goldens).
- Full `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` run on this branch: 3141 pass, 44 fail.
  The same suite on the same tree with these changes stashed gives 3140 pass,
  43 fail, and the two failure sets are identical except for one
  load-sensitive update-notifier lease test that passes when it is re-run in
  isolation. The shared failures are pre-existing Windows-environment ones
  (symlink/EPERM, path separators) and do not touch repository evidence.
- Two independent reviews of the diff; the findings about the invalid example
  path, the contradicting paragraph, the missing changelog entry, the message
  wording, the missing negative cases and the duplicated host table were
  applied.

## Scope and limits

- The declaration is trusted exactly as the accepted GitLab precedent trusts
  it: Archify never contacts the host to detect its forge. A wrong
  declaration can only produce broken links; verification still runs against
  the local checkout, and a web link is only built for a revision, path and
  line range that were verified there.
- A GitHub-family repository path is `owner/repository`; nested groups remain
  GitLab-only, and a host on a non-standard HTTPS port still has no web links.
- The explainer still derives `link_mode: "local-only"` for an unrecognised
  origin, because it does not pass a provider hint — unchanged behaviour, the
  same gap the self-managed GitLab case has today. An explainer document that
  declares `meta.repository.provider` explicitly does get links.

## Refresh onto the current `dev`

- Rebased onto `dev` @ `7b4ebba9`; the only conflict was the packaged archive `archify.zip`, rebuilt from the merged tree with the canonical Node 22 toolchain (two builds, byte-identical, sha256 `76a6fe5048f8769a1fcae75826757c2fec8d8a1865908a6277eb2cad48001bb6`).
- New head `ade96ef7`. The focused suite and `npm run test:generated` are green on the refreshed branch.

owners.title: Add Verifiable Source Evidence to Architecture Relationships
owners.scope:
## Problem

Architecture diagrams can identify repository-backed components, but component-level source evidence does not necessarily explain why a particular relationship exists.

At development baseline `500d4a65211ffe607fde6b3ce7505027b45bb59e`, the Architecture connection schema rejects a `sources` property, while the shared repository-evidence collector enumerates Architecture components rather than connections.

A minimal CLI reproduction confirms that adding `sources` to `/connections/0` fails with `schema/additionalProperties`. As a result, an authored relationship can be displayed without a first-class, verifiable source reference attached to that relationship.

## Proposed solution

Extend the existing revision-pinned repository-evidence contract to support optional source evidence on Architecture connections.

Reuse the existing evidence representation, repository identity, pinned-commit validation, path-safety checks, and line-range validation wherever possible. Expose verified relationship evidence through the standalone Viewer without changing the authored topology or canonical diagram geometry.

Coordinate with PR #1063 before modifying the shared repository-evidence pipeline.

## Scope

- Add an optional, backward-compatible connection evidence representation.
- Validate connection evidence through the existing repository-evidence pipeline.
- Expose verified evidence in relationship inspection.
- Distinguish verified, missing, and invalid evidence.
- Preserve existing node evidence behavior and other renderer contracts.

## Non-goals

- Automatically inferring relationships.
- Treating source references as proof of runtime execution or causality.
- Automatically crawling repositories.
- Introducing runtime network requests.
- Requiring evidence on existing diagrams.
- Building a parallel source-verification implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- A valid connection source resolves to the declared repository revision, file, and permitted line range.
- Invalid revisions, paths, and line ranges produce actionable diagnostics.
- Existing diagrams without connection evidence continue to validate and render.
- Adding evidence does not change relationship endpoints, direction, topology, routing, or canonical SVG geometry.
- Existing Architecture node evidence remains compatible.
- Other supported renderer types retain their existing evidence behavior.
- No runtime network request is introduced.
- A real standalone HTML example, negative fixtures, and concise browser evidence are provided.
- Automated results and human visual acceptance are reported separately.

## Implementation checklist

- [ ] Coordinate the schema and shared-validator boundary with PR #1063.
- [ ] Agree on the smallest compatible connection evidence representation.
- [ ] Extend evidence validation and verified payload collection.
- [ ] Add relationship-level evidence inspection in the Viewer.
- [ ] Add invalid-evidence and legacy-input regression fixtures.
- [ ] Run the required test suite and cross-renderer regression checks.
- [ ] Attach reproducible HTML and concise review evidence.

## Open design question

Should connection evidence reuse the existing source-reference structure unchanged, or does the current payload require a minimal extension? Prefer reuse unless a concrete incompatibility is demonstrated.
